new.title: Endovascular therapy for mild-to-moderate stroke due to basilar artery occlusion: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
new.abstract: [BACKGROUND] Endovascular therapy (EVT) is an established treatment for basilar artery occlusion (BAO) with severe deficits, but its benefit in patients with mild-to-moderate symptoms (National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale [NIHSS] <10) remains unclear due to limited randomized controlled trial (RCT) evidence. We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis to evaluate EVT efficacy and safety in this subgroup. [METHODS] We searched PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library for RCTs and observational studies published between January 1, 2014, and July 1, 2026, comparing EVT plus best medical treatment (BMT) versus BMT in BAO with NIHSS <10. new.title: Compared strategies of carotid revascularization periprocedural risks and long-term outcomes: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized trials of stenting versus endarterectomy.
new.abstract: [OBJECTIVE] Carotid endarterectomy (CEA) remains the benchmark open revascularization strategy for appropriately selected patients with extracranial carotid stenosis, whereas carotid artery stenting (CAS) provides an endovascular alternative when cervical exposure, medical comorbidity, or anatomic factors make open surgery less favorable. Balancing periprocedural stroke, myocardial infarction, cranial nerve injury, and long-term stroke risk remains central to contemporary cerebrovascular decision-making. This study compared periprocedural and exploratory long-term outcomes after CAS versus CEA using randomized head-to-head trial evidence across trial eras. [OBJECTIVE] To compare stroke, death, and functional disability following microsurgical resection versus conservative management in patients with unruptured brain arteriovenous malformations (AVMs). [METHODS] A PROSPERO-registered systematic review and meta-analysis (CRD420261354328) searched six databases from January 2014 through March 2026. new.abstract: Sylvian-fissure-region arteriovenous malformations (AVMs) are uncommon and anatomically heterogeneous; published labels often describe non-comparable lesions or populations. To update evidence for microsurgery, stereotactic radiosurgery (SRS), and endovascular treatment (EVT). Following PRISMA 2020, five databases were searched through May 2026 with citation chaining. Two reviewers independently screened records and extracted data. Dedicated sylvian/perisylvian cohorts were distinguished from broader cohorts and contextual technical reports. Incompatible endpoints, non-independent arms, and potentially overlapping cohorts were not pooled. new.title: Hypoglossal-facial nerve anastomosis for facial nerve injury after vestibular schwannoma surgery: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
new.abstract: [BACKGROUND] Facial nerve injury is one of the most common and distressing complications following vestibular schwannoma (VS) surgery. Hypoglossal-facial nerve anastomosis (HFA) is a nerve repair technique used in patients with facial nerve injury. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the techniques, outcomes, and complications of HFA for facial nerve injury following VS resection. [METHODS] A systematic search of PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Herdin databases was conducted from inception to September 2025. Studies were included if they reported HFA for facial nerve injury after VS surgery. new.title: Effectiveness and cost-effectiveness of epilepsy surgery in patients with refractory epilepsy: A systematic review of decision-analytic models.
new.abstract: Our objective was to evaluate the effectiveness and cost-effectiveness of epilepsy surgery for the treatment of patients with DRE. We carried out a systematic review of Decision Analytic Models (DAMs) in the main international databases regarding the comparison between epilepsy surgery versus medical treatment. We evaluated the relevance and credibility of the DAMs with the ISPOR-AMCP-NPC tool. We synthesized the results qualitatively. The certainty of the body of evidence was determined using the GRADE approach proposed for modeling studies. new.abstract: [BACKGROUND] Microvascular decompression (MVD) for glossopharyngeal neuralgia (GPN) presumes a compressive neurovascular conflict at the glossopharyngeal-vagal root entry zone, but the distribution of offending vessels has never been quantified across series. [OBJECTIVE] To estimate the pooled prevalence of each offending vessel identified at MVD for GPN, alongside pain relief, recurrence, mortality and complications. [METHODS] PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science and Cochrane CENTRAL were searched from inception through August 2026. Studies with at least five GPN patients undergoing MVD and extractable outcomes were included. new.abstract: [BACKGROUND] Endovascular thrombectomy is an established treatment for acute ischemic stroke. Whether the benefit extends to patients with salvageable brain tissue in the infarct who present more than 24 hours after symptom onset or the time when they were last known to be well is uncertain. [METHODS] We conducted an open-label, randomized trial with blinded outcome assessment at comprehensive stroke centers in China. Patients with acute ischemic stroke from large-vessel occlusion of the anterior circulation and imaging-identified salvageable brain tissue at 24 to 72 hours were assigned to receive endovascular therapy plus standard medical care (intervention group) or standard medical care alone (control group). popular.abstract: [BACKGROUND] The safety of omitting up-front treatment with aspirin during primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) in patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) remains unclear. [METHODS] We conducted a multicenter, open-label, randomized trial in Japan involving patients with STEMI who were undergoing primary PCI. new.abstract: [OBJECTIVES] Machine-learning and deep-learning approaches have been successfully applied to EEG-based prognostication in comatose patients after cardiac arrest (CA), but typically rely on task-specific signal processing, feature extraction, and model development. Here, we investigated whether two commercially available multimodal large language models (LLMs) could predict neurological outcome directly from EEG images. [METHODS] Thirty-three comatose patients on the first day after CA from a prospective cohort were included. For each patient, a single 10-second EEG segment displayed using a longitudinal bipolar montage was rendered as PNG image. new.title: Brain2voice 2.0: High-performance voice synthesis brain-computer interface.
new.abstract: Brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) offer a promising solution to speech loss due to neurological injury by decoding intended speech directly from brain activity. While recent BCIs have restored high-accuracy text-based communication, they fail to provide instantaneous voice output essential for the natural flow of conversation. Brain-to-voice BCIs address this gap by decoding voice directly from neural signals. However, even the state-of-the-art (SOTA) BCI-synthesized voice is not yet intelligible enough for real-world adoption. We introduce brain2voice 2.0, a new multimodal Transformer-based BCI decoder architecture capable of synthesizing highly intelligible voice from intracortical neural signals in real-time. This study examined whether a convolutional neural network trained exclusively on resting-state EEG could preserve task-relevant information when transferred to previously unseen N-back working memory tasks without task-specific fine-tuning.Approach. new.title: A User-Function Taxonomy for Brain-Computer Interfaces: From Task Definition to Evidence.
new.abstract: Brain-computer interface (BCI) studies are commonly compared by electrode, signal, paradigm, device, or clinical purpose. These descriptors do not identify the user-level function implemented in a task, although that function determines the appropriate endpoint. This article proposes the Type-Wield-Synthesize-Sense (TWSS) framework as a complementary taxonomy. Type involves selecting one option from alternatives specified before a decision. Wield regulates an observable state that remains correctable over time. Synthesize infers intentional expressive content without presenting alternatives at each update. new.abstract: Brain-computer interface (BCI) technology serves as an important bridge between the nervous system and external devices and has shown considerable promise for the diagnosis and treatment of neurodegenerative diseases, whose global burden continues to increase: in 2021, more than 57 million people were living with dementia worldwide, with Alzheimer's disease (AD) accounting for approximately 60-70% of cases, while an estimated 11.77 million people were living with Parkinson's disease (PD) in 2021, according to the Global Burden of Disease Study 2021. new.abstract: [OBJECTIVE] This study developed neurophysiologically informed data augmentation strategies to improve electroencephalogram (EEG)-based deep learning classification of attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) in children with limited labeled EEG data. ADHD affects approximately 8.0% of children and adolescents worldwide, or about 129 million individuals aged 5-19 years. Clinical diagnosis relies largely on behavioral observations; EEG provides objective biomarkers, but conventional image augmentation may not preserve disease-relevant neural oscillation patterns. new.title: EEG-based deep learning reveals cortical sensitivity to small changes in deep brain stimulation parameters.
new.abstract: Deep Brain Stimulation (DBS) is an invasive procedure used to alleviate motor symptoms in Parkinson's Disease (PD) patients. Despite its effectiveness, the impact of DBS on brain activity and the way to optimise stimulation parameters remains unclear. In this study, we aimed to map the sensitivity of cortical neural response to changes in DBS parameters in real-world clinical settings. We recorded in-clinic EEG data from PD patients during their clinical DBS programming sessions, both at rest and during arm movement. new.abstract: This study evaluated personalized gait phase estimation for stroke survivors using functional inertial measurement unit (IMU) alignment and two-stage supervised personalization of models pre-trained on healthy gait. Stage 1 established a distillation-regularized participant-specific model, and Stage 2 performed conditional refinement using low-rank adaptation. new.abstract: Upper-limb motor impairments associated with neurological disorders such as cerebral palsy (CP) are characterized by abnormal muscle coordination, spasticity, fatigue, and highly variable electromyographic (EMG) patterns, posing significant challenges for rehabilitation exoskeleton control. While EMG-driven and adaptive controllers have shown promise, existing approaches often rely on fixed gains or address physiological state estimation, prediction, and decision-making in isolation, limiting robustness and clinical relevance-particularly in pediatric populations. Increasing evidence showed that radiomics and Deep Learning (DL) may improve diagnostic objectivity by extracting quantitative features from MRI data. This study aimed to synthesize the evidence on the diagnostic performance and clinical utility of these models. [METHODS] a systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted following PRISMA-DTA guidelines and PRISMA 2020 recommendations: PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science databases from inception to December 2025. new.title: Unimodal imaging foundation models and vision-language models in MRI: A systematic review of emerging methods and clinical applications.
new.abstract: Artificial intelligence in medical imaging is shifting from task-specific algorithms toward adaptable foundation models (FMs) and vision-language models (VLMs). However, applying these models to MRI remains challenging because clinical interpretation requires integrating multi-parametric, volumetric imaging across multiple sequences with clinical context. This systematic review evaluates 35 studies on unimodal FMs and multimodal VLMs in MRI, summarizing emerging architectures, downstream applications, and challenges to clinical translation. Current research is concentrated in neuroimaging, with diagnostic classification representing the most mature application. new.abstract: [BACKGROUND] Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly integrated into healthcare information systems, supporting clinical decision-making, imaging analysis, and predictive modeling. While these applications offer operational and clinical benefits, they also introduce emerging risks to patient privacy, data security, and system reliability. [OBJECTIVE] To systematically review empirical evidence on privacy breaches, security vulnerabilities, and misuse associated with AI applications in healthcare settings. [METHODS] PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Scopus, IEEE Xplore, and ACM Digital Library were searched for empirical studies published between January 2015 and November 2025 that evaluated AI use or misuse in clinical diagnosis, treatment, or decision-making. new.abstract: [BACKGROUND] Accurately distinguishing malignant pleural effusion (MPE) from non-malignant pleural effusion is clinically important, but the generalisability and methodological quality of machine-learning (ML) models remain uncertain. [METHODS] We searched eight databases to 23 April 2026. Diagnostic performance was pooled using random-effects and Reitsma bivariate models, and study quality was assessed using PROBAST+AI. new.abstract: [BACKGROUND] Antidepressant selection is constrained by limited comparative-effectiveness data, with randomized trials measuring symptom reduction rather than patient-reported tolerability. We tested whether AI-assisted analysis of patient-written online reviews recovers drug-level tolerability signals that converge with the strongest randomized evidence. [METHODS] We did a cross-sectional analysis of 8348 reviews of 16 antidepressants for major depressive disorder posted to Drugs.com (February 2008-March 2025; ≥1 month reported use). new.title: Fully Automated Segmentation of Chronic Total Occlusion Lesions on Coronary CT Angiography Using Deep Learning.
new.abstract: Reliable quantitative assessment for chronic total occlusion (CTO) lesions depends on accurate segmentation of coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) images. However, incomplete contrast opacification and complex lesion morphology make precise delineation particularly challenging. We developed an Atrous Attention U-Net (AAU-Net) for CTO segmentation and integrated it into a fully automated workflow comprising heart localization, CTO localization, and lesion segmentation. This retrospective study included 565 CTO lesions from 551 patients who underwent prospectively ECG-gated CCTA at three centers. new.title: Interpretable deep learning maps spatial morphological phenotypes to HCC and LUAD survival.
new.abstract: The clinical adoption of deep learning in pathology is largely hindered by the "black box" nature of current models, which often obscure the biological basis of prognosis. Here, we introduce MorphX, an interpretable framework that predicts patient survival by explicitly decoding multi-scale morphological patterns from whole-slide images. Unlike conventional methods relying on latent features, MorphX fuses macro-scale tissue texture with micro-scale nuclear metrics to attribute risk to interpretable biological phenotypes. In a multi-center study spanning 1,067 patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD), MorphX achieves concordance indices of 0.775-0.799 in discovery cohorts. new.title: AI-based prediction of actionable genomic alterations from H&E-stained slides.
new.abstract: Precision oncology based on the identification of actionable genomic alterations (AGAs) has been transformative in the care of solid tumors, yet optimal treatment selection is often hindered by tissue exhaustion and slow turnaround times. Artificial intelligence (AI) addresses these barriers by predicting AGAs directly from routine hematoxylin and eosin (H&E)-stained slides. Recent landmark studies, including the prospective EAGLE and ANNAR trials, have demonstrated that deep learning models can identify alterations such as EGFR in non-small cell lung cancer and FGFR in urothelial cancer across diverse global cohorts. ns.abstract: [BACKGROUND] Percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) is increasingly used for revascularization of unprotected left main coronary artery disease. Whether intravascular ultrasonographic (IVUS) guidance during PCI results in better clinical outcomes than conventional angiographic guidance alone is uncertain. [METHODS] In an international, multicenter, open-label trial, we randomly assigned patients with unprotected left main coronary artery disease in a 1:1 ratio to undergo either IVUS-guided PCI or angiography-guided PCI. The primary end point was a patient-oriented composite of any stroke, any myocardial infarction, any revascularization, or death from any cause at the longest follow-up. ns.title: The Safety and Outcomes of Elective Endovascular Aneurysm Repair in the Elderly: A Systemic Review and Meta-Analysis.
ns.abstract: [PURPOSE] Prevalence of abdominal aortic aneurysms (AAAs) increases with age. Previous trials confirm that elective endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR) is an effective intervention for AAA. However, few elderly patients were recruited into randomized trials, whereas in contemporary clinical practice, elective repair is commonly performed on octogenarians. We evaluated the safety and outcome of elective EVAR in elderly patients to inform clinical practice and vascular service provision. bmi.abstract: Electroencephalography-based brain-computer interfaces have revolutionized the integration of neural signals with technological systems, offering transformative solutions across neuroscience, biomedical engineering, and clinical practice. This review systematically analyzes advancements in electroencephalography-based brain-computer interface architectures, emphasizing four pillars, namely signal acquisition, paradigm design, decoding algorithms, and diverse applications. The aim is to bridge the gap between technology and application and guide future research. bmi.abstract: Previous research has demonstrated the potential of using pre-trained language models for decoding open vocabulary Electroencephalography (EEG) signals captured through a non-invasive Brain-Computer Interface (BCI). ai.abstract: [INTRODUCTION] Prediabetes is a prevalent condition in which early detection and lifestyle interventions can prevent or delay progression to diabetes. Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) offer enhanced tools for diagnosis, risk stratification, and scalable delivery of lifestyle interventions. This review synthesizes current applications of AI/ML in patients with prediabetes. [METHODS] We conducted a scoping review using PubMed, EMBASE, and Web of Science (through May 2025) to identify original studies applying AI/ML to prediabetes prediction or management. ai.abstract: Epicardial adipose tissue (EAT) and pericardial adipose tissue (PAT) are increasingly recognized as distinct fat depots with implications for cardiovascular disease. This review discusses their anatomical and physiological characteristics, as well as their pathophysiological roles. EAT, in direct contact with the myocardium, exerts local inflammatory and metabolic effects on the heart, while PAT influences cardiovascular health rather systemically. We sought to discuss the currently used imaging modalities to assess these fat compartments-CT, MRI, and echocardiography-emphasizing their advantages, limitations, and the urgent need for standardization for both scanning and image reconstruction. ai.title: Autonomous biomedical research with an artificial intelligence agent.
ai.abstract: Biomedical research is increasingly constrained by repetitive, fragmented workflows that slow discovery. We introduce Biomni, a general-purpose biomedical artificial intelligence agent that autonomously executes diverse research tasks. To map the biomedical action space, Biomni's action-discovery agent mines tools, databases, and protocols from thousands of publications across 25 domains, building a unified agentic environment. Its general-purpose architecture integrates large language model reasoning with retrieval-augmented planning and code-based execution, dynamically composing workflows without predefined templates. ai.title: A deep learning framework for efficient pathology image analysis.
ai.abstract: Artificial intelligence has transformed digital pathology by enabling biomarker prediction from high-resolution whole-slide images. However, current methods are computationally inefficient, processing thousands of redundant tiles per slide and requiring complex aggregation models. We introduce EAGLE (Efficient Approach for Guided Local Examination), a deep learning framework that emulates pathologists by selectively analyzing informative regions. EAGLE combines task-agnostic tile selection with detailed feature extraction and is benchmarked against leading slide- and tile-level foundation models across 43 tasks from nine cancer types spanning morphology, biomarker prediction, treatment response and prognosis. ai.title: Deep learning electrocardiogram model for risk stratification of coronary revascularization need in the emergency department.
ai.abstract: [BACKGROUND AND AIMS] Identification of patients with acute coronary syndrome requiring coronary revascularization can be challenging due to inconclusive electrocardiogram (ECG) findings or biomarker results. A deep learning model to detect ECG patterns associated with revascularization likelihood was developed, aiming to guide further assessment and reduce diagnostic uncertainty. [METHODS] A convolutional neural network model was trained on 144 691 ED visits from a US cohort (60 ± 19 years; 53% female; 0.6% revascularization), tested on a separate test cohort (n = 35 995), and benchmarked against clinician ECG interpretation and cardiac troponin T (TnT). ai.title: Foundation models for radiology: fundamentals, applications, opportunities, challenges, risks, and prospects.
ai.abstract: Foundation models (FMs) represent a significant evolution in artificial intelligence (AI), impacting diverse fields. Within radiology, this evolution offers greater adaptability, multimodal integration, and improved generalizability compared with traditional narrow AI. Utilizing large-scale pre-training and efficient fine-tuning, FMs can support diverse applications, including image interpretation, report generation, integrative diagnostics combining imaging with clinical/laboratory data, and synthetic data creation, holding significant promise for advancements in precision medicine. However, clinical translation of FMs faces several substantial challenges. ai.title: Human versus artificial intelligence: evaluating ChatGPT's performance in conducting published systematic reviews with meta-analysis in chronic pain research.
ai.abstract: [INTRODUCTION] Artificial intelligence (AI), particularly large-language models like Chat Generative Pre-Trained Transformer (ChatGPT), has demonstrated potential in streamlining research methodologies. Systematic reviews and meta-analyses, often considered the pinnacle of evidence-based medicine, are inherently time-intensive and demand meticulous planning, rigorous data extraction, thorough analysis, and careful synthesis. Despite promising applications of AI, its utility in conducting systematic reviews with meta-analysis remains unclear. This study evaluated ChatGPT's accuracy in conducting key tasks of a systematic review with meta-analysis.
